term: moved by nature, moved by force (φύσει, βίᾳ καὶ παρὰ φύσιν)
definition: A thing is moved by nature in a respect when the source of that motion is in it, as fire moves up and an animal moves itself; it is moved by force and contrary to nature when it is moved against that source, as earth moved up (Physics VIII.4, 254b12-24). Lean: the primitives `ByNature` and `ByForce` of TruthCore.Greek.Aristotle.Physics.Typed; nothing defines them.
